body: Which feature of the first trial did the organisers intend to address by proposing a same-day second trial?
options: The map versions contained different information.
The maps were handed out on different days when different galleries were open.
Volunteers did not record how often visitors asked for directions.
Both map versions were withdrawn after the first trial.
explanation: The organisers noted that the map versions were handed out on different days, when different galleries were open. Distributing both versions on the same day was proposed to help separate the effect of lettering from differences between the days.
passage_text: In a fictional exhibition, visitors received either a printed map or a map containing the same information with larger lettering. Volunteers recorded how often each group asked for directions. Those receiving the larger lettering asked less often. The organisers noted that volunteers had handed out the maps on different days, when different galleries were open. They proposed a second trial in which both versions would be distributed on the same day. Meanwhile, both maps remained available. The first trial provided a reason to investigate readability, but it could not separate the effect of lettering from differences between the days.

body: An office stopped using its old filing device because a newly invented electronic system now performs the same task. The old device still works. Which word is closest in meaning to “obsolete” as used here?
explanation: “Obsolete” describes something no longer used because something new has been invented. “Superseded” is closest here: the office no longer uses the working device because the new system performs its task.
evidence_quotes: no longer used because something new has been invented
stated_assumptions: The office stopped using the device because the newly invented system performs the same task.
The old device still works.
option_analysis: A. “Inoperative” does not fit because the stem states that the device still works.
B. “Traditional” does not express that the device is no longer used because a new system was invented.
C. “Superseded” fits the stated situation: the new system performs the task, and the office no longer uses the old device.
D. “Scarce” does not express the stated reason the office stopped using the device.
subject: english

reasons: The excerpt defines “obsolete” as no longer used because something new has been invented. The new electronic system replaces the still-working filing device, so “superseded” (C) is the closest option.
A is contradicted by the device still working; B means traditional or customary, not replaced; D means scarce or in short supply.
Quality score 8/10

body:
The following four complete sentences describe one fictional class project. Arrange them in the order that makes their references and timing cues coherent.
(A) Only after the paper covering was attached and the adhesive had dried did Tara place the photographs on the board.
(B) Tara began by measuring the display board's width.
(C) She used that measurement to cut paper to fit the board.
(D) She attached the cut paper to the board and waited for the adhesive to dry.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: Tara must measure the board before using that measurement to cut the paper. She attaches the cut paper and waits for the adhesive to dry before placing the photographs, so the coherent order is B-C-D-A.
evidence_quotes: In a fictional class project, Tara first measured the width of the display board. Using that measurement, she cut a sheet of paper to fit it. She then attached the cut sheet to the board and let the adhesive dry. Only after it had dried did she arrange the photographs on the covered board. The account describes that
sequence explicitly; it does not prescribe a universal method of preparing every display.
stated_assumptions: The temporal cues in the four sentences indicate the order of events in this fictional project.
The pronoun "She" in sentence (C) refers to Tara, and the references to the board and cut paper in sentence (D) refer to the display board and paper in the earlier sentences.
option_analysis: B-C-D-A is correct: it places measuring before cutting, cutting before attaching, and attaching and drying before placing the photographs.
B-D-C-A places attachment before cutting, although the paper is cut to fit before it is attached.
C-B-D-A uses the measurement before the sentence that establishes it.
B-C-A-D places the photographs before the attachment-and-drying step, despite the explicit timing cue in sentence (A).

body:
The following four complete sentences describe one fictional account. Arrange them in the order that forms a coherent account.
(A) Only after comparing the edited copy with the untouched original did Aman save the edited version under a different name.
(B) Aman found background noise in the recording of his interview.
(C) He first made a copy of the original recording.
(D) He reduced the noise by editing that copy.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: Sentence B introduces the recording problem, and sentence C states that Aman first made a copy. Sentence D edits that copy; sentence A then refers to the edited copy and places the comparison before saving it.
evidence_quotes: In this fictional account, Aman found that the recording of his interview contained background noise. He first made a copy of the original recording. He then edited the copy to reduce the noise. After editing it, he compared the copy with the untouched original. Finally, he saved the edited version under a different
name. The original was retained throughout the stated process.
stated_assumptions: All four sentences describe the same fictional account.
Temporal expressions such as “first” and “only after” indicate the order of events.
“That copy” and “the edited copy” refer to the copy made from the original recording.
option_analysis: Correct: B introduces the noise, C gives the copying step, D describes editing the copy, and A places comparison before saving.
Incorrect: This puts editing before the copy is made, although the account states that Aman first made a copy and then edited it.
Incorrect: This puts making the copy before the account introduces the background-noise problem.
Incorrect: This puts the saving of the edited version before the editing step.

body:
Match each case in List-I with the word in List-II that best fits the stated feature. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) A troubleshooting guide arranges its instructions logically, making them easy to follow.
(B) A meeting record retains only necessary and important information, expressed in a few words.
(C) In a wide region, trees are present in small numbers and are spread far apart.
(D) A cartographer checks every symbol and label on a map, paying careful attention to each detail.

List-II
(I) "Concise" — giving only the information that is necessary and important, using few words
(II) "Sparse" — only present in small amounts or numbers and often spread over a large area
(III) "Meticulous" — paying careful attention to every detail
(IV) "Coherent" — logical and well organized; easy to understand and clear

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The guide is coherent because its instructions are logically arranged and easy to follow. The meeting record is concise because it gives necessary information in a few words, while the widely spaced trees are sparse. The cartographer is meticulous because the description states that every map detail is checked carefully.
evidence_quotes: logical and well organized; easy to understand and clear
giving only the information that is necessary and important, using few words
only present in small amounts or numbers and often spread over a large area
paying careful attention to every detail
stated_assumptions: Use only the feature stated in each case; each word in List-II is to be used once.
option_analysis: Option A is incorrect: it matches the logically ordered guide with "Sparse" and the widely spaced trees with "Coherent", reversing those descriptions.
Option B is correct: it matches the guide with "Coherent", the brief meeting record with "Concise", the trees with "Sparse", and the careful map-checking with "Meticulous".
Option C is incorrect: it matches the meeting record with "Meticulous" and the map-checking with "Concise", which do not fit the stated features.
Option D is incorrect: it matches the guide with "Concise" and the meeting record with "Coherent", confusing logical organisation with brevity.

A farm stopped using its hand-operated seed drill after it broke; no new sowing machine had been invented, yet the drill was obsolete.
A farm found its hand-operated seed drill slow to operate but continued using it; the drill was obsolete.
explanation: In A, the farm no longer uses the hand-operated drill because a newly invented drill replaced it, which matches the stated sense of "obsolete". B and D say the drill remains in use, while C attributes its non-use to a breakdown and states that no new sowing machine had been invented.

options: The maps carried different information, so content differences could explain the groups’ questions.

The first trial provided a reason to investigate readability, but it could not separate the effect of lettering from differences between the days.

body: Which conclusion about the first trial is best supported by the passage?
options: The lettering was the only difference between the groups of visitors.
Larger lettering caused visitors to ask for directions less often.
Differences between the days did not affect the comparison.
Visitors with larger-letter maps asked less often, but the trial did not isolate the effect of lettering.
explanation: The passage reports that visitors receiving larger-letter maps asked for directions less often. It also states that the maps were handed out on different days, when different galleries were open, so the first trial could not isolate the effect of lettering. Option D reports the observed difference without claiming that lettering caused it.
passage_text: In a fictional exhibition, visitors received either a printed map or a map containing the same information with larger lettering. Volunteers recorded how often each group asked for directions. Those receiving the larger lettering asked less often. The organisers noted that volunteers had handed out the maps on different days, when different galleries were open. They proposed a second trial in which both versions would be distributed on the same day. Meanwhile, both maps remained available. The first trial provided a reason to investigate readability, but it could not separate the effect of lettering from differences between the days.

body: For several weeks, the crew carried heavy supplies up a steep route each day, with little time to rest. The supervisor described the assignment as "arduous". Which word is closest in meaning to "arduous" as used here?
explanation: The repeated carrying of heavy supplies with little rest over several weeks involves sustained effort and energy. “Arduous” means involving a lot of effort and energy, especially over a period of time, so “demanding” is the closest match.
evidence_quotes: involving a lot of effort and energy, especially over a period of time
stated_assumptions: The repeated carrying and limited rest represent sustained effort over several weeks.
Technical complexity and emotional unpleasantness are not intended as defining features of the assignment.
option_analysis: A is correct: "demanding" captures the sustained effort described in the stem.
B describes the assignment's duration, but duration alone does not capture the effort in the definition of "arduous".
C suggests complexity, which the stem does not establish as the assignment's defining feature.
D describes an emotional quality that is not established as the meaning of "arduous" in the excerpt.

body:
Arrange the following four sentences to form a coherent account.
(A) Only then did the class vote on the listed titles.
(B) In a fictional class, the teacher first asked pupils to propose titles for a shared story.
(C) After the votes had been counted, she wrote the selected title on the story's cover.

body:
Match each word in List-I with its meaning in List-II.

List-I
(A) concise
(B) authentic
(C) sceptical
(D) sparse

List-II
(I) known to be real and what somebody claims it is, and not a copy
(II) giving only the information that is necessary and important, using few words
(III) having doubts that a claim or statement is true or that something will happen
(IV) only present in small amounts or numbers and often spread over a large area

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Concise means giving only necessary and important information using few words, while authentic means known to be real and not a copy. Sceptical describes having doubts about whether a claim or statement is true, and sparse describes something present in small amounts or numbers, often spread over a large area. These meanings give the mapping A-II, B-I, C-III and D-IV.

Incorrect. B is correctly matched, but A uses few words rather than many; C includes unrelated information rather than only necessary information; and D is lengthy rather than including unrelated information.
Incorrect. A includes no unrelated information, B is brief rather than lengthy, C does not omit a stated necessary detail, and D is lengthy rather than brief.

body: Choose the sentence in which "elated" is used correctly.
options: After hearing that her application had been rejected, Asha felt elated, although she was disappointed and not happy or excited about the result.

body: Which feature was identical in the two map versions?
options: The two versions were distributed on the same day.
Both versions were unavailable during the first trial.
The two versions contained the same information.
The two versions were distributed when the same galleries were open.
explanation: The passage states that the map with larger lettering contained the same information as the printed map. It also says the maps were distributed on different days and that both versions remained available.
passage_text: In a fictional exhibition, visitors received either a printed map or a map containing the same information with larger lettering. Volunteers recorded how often each group asked for directions. Those receiving the larger lettering asked less often. The organisers noted that volunteers had handed out the maps on different days, when different galleries were open. They proposed a second trial in which both versions would be distributed on the same day. Meanwhile, both maps remained available. The first trial provided a reason to investigate readability, but it could not separate the effect of lettering from differences between the days.

body: A company issued shares at a premium. Before the shares were validly forfeited for non-payment of a call, the entire premium due on them had been received and recorded. What should be done with the recorded share-premium entry when the shares are forfeited?
options: Transfer the recorded premium amount to Share Forfeiture Account.
Leave the recorded share-premium entry unchanged.
Debit the recorded premium amount to Share Capital Account.
explanation: On forfeiture, entries relating to the shares are reversed except the entry for share premium already received. Since the stem states that the entire premium was received and recorded before forfeiture, that entry remains unchanged.
evidence_quotes: 38 Accountancy : Company Accounts and Analysis of Financial Statements It may be noted here that when the shares are forfeited, all entries relating to the forfeited shares must be reversed except the entry relating to share premium received, if any.
stated_assumptions: The shares were issued at a premium, and the entire premium due was received and recorded before forfeiture.
The shares were validly forfeited for non-payment of a call under the company's articles.
The question concerns only the recorded entry for the premium received.
option_analysis: A is incorrect because the recorded entry for premium received is excepted from reversal.
B is incorrect because transferring the amount would alter the premium entry rather than leave it unchanged.
C is correct because the recorded entry for premium received is not reversed on forfeiture.
D is incorrect because debiting Share Capital Account would alter the premium entry rather than leave it unchanged.
subject: accountancy
topic: Financial Statements of Company: focus on this supplied section: 1.7 Forfeiture of Shares It may happen that some shareholders fail to pay one or more instalments, viz. allotment money and/or call money. reasons: C is correct: the excerpts state that on forfeiture, entries are reversed except for the entry relating to share premium already received. Since the stem says the entire premium was received and recorded, leave that entry unchanged.

The stem explicitly supplies the decisive case conditions: shares were issued at a premium, forfeiture was valid, and the entire premium was received and recorded before forfeiture.

body: A company issues 15,000 shares of face value ₹10 each at par. It receives applications for 18,000 shares, and all 15,000 shares offered are allotted. The company calls ₹8 per allotted share. Holders of 600 allotted shares pay only ₹5 per share against this call; holders of all the remaining allotted shares pay the full amount called. There are no other unpaid calls. What is the paid-up share capital at this stage?
explanation: Called-up capital is 15,000 × ₹8 = ₹1,20,000. Calls in arrears are 600 × (₹8 − ₹5) = ₹1,800. Paid-up capital is called-up capital less calls in arrears: ₹1,20,000 − ₹1,800 = ₹1,18,200.

body:
A company collects capital from a very large number of persons. No separate capital account is opened for each person; their contributions are combined in one common capital account. Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) The persons contributing capital
(B) The amount contributed by those persons
(C) The common account in which the contributions are combined
(D) The stated reason for not opening a separate capital account for each person

List-II
(I) Share Capital Account
(II) Shareholders
(III) Share capital
(IV) The very large number of shareholders

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The persons contributing capital are shareholders, and the amount they contribute is share capital. Since the number of shareholders is very large, their contributions are combined in a common Share Capital Account rather than recorded in separate capital accounts; therefore, the correct mapping is (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV).
evidence_quotes: 1.3 Share Capital of a Company A company, being an artificial person, cannot generate its own capital which has necessarily to be collected from several persons. These persons are known as shareholders and the amount contributed by them is called share capital. Since the number of shareholders is very very large, a

separate capital account cannot be opened for each one of them. Hence, innumerable streams of capital contribution merge their identities in a common capital account called as ‘Share Capital Account’. Reprint 2026-27
stated_assumptions: The persons described in the case are the persons contributing to the company's capital.
The common account in the case records the combined contributions, and no separate capital account is opened for each contributor.
option_analysis: Incorrect: it interchanges the persons contributing capital and the amount contributed.
Incorrect: it matches the common account with the large number of shareholders and the stated reason with the account name.
Correct: it matches the contributors, their contribution, the common account and the reason for using that account.
Incorrect: it matches the contributed amount with the account name and the common account with share capital.

body:
A non-financial enterprise prepares a cash flow statement. Each transaction below is a cash transaction. The dividend is received from an investment in another enterprise. The shares mentioned in (C) and the debt instruments mentioned in (D) relate to another enterprise; the shares are held for trading purposes, and the debt instruments are not held for trading purposes. None of the investments or instruments mentioned is included in cash equivalents. Select the correct statements.
(A) Cash interest received on loans and advances made to third parties is an investing cash outflow.
(B) A cash dividend received from an investment in another enterprise is an investing cash inflow.
(C) A cash payment to acquire shares held for trading purposes is classified as an investing cash outflow.
(D) A cash payment to acquire debt instruments not held for trading purposes is classified as an investing cash outflow.
explanation: Cash interest received from loans and advances and cash dividends received from investments are investing cash inflows, so (A) is incorrect and (B) is correct. A cash payment to acquire debt instruments of another enterprise is an investing outflow when those instruments are not held for trading purposes, making (D) correct. Shares held for trading purposes are excluded from the stated investing outflows, so (C) is incorrect.

6.5.2 Cash from Investing Activities As per AS-3, investing activities are the acquisition and disposal of long-term assets and other investments not included in cash equivalents. Investing activities relate to purchase and sale of long-term assets or fixed assets such Reprint 2026-27
stated_assumptions: All listed receipts and payments are cash transactions.
The dividend, shares and debt instruments relate to another enterprise.
The shares in statement (C) are held for trading; the debt instruments in statement (D) are not held for trading.
option_analysis: Incorrect: the excerpt identifies cash interest received on loans and advances as an investing inflow, not an outflow.
Incorrect: although the direction in (A) is wrong, statement (D) is also correct because the debt instruments are not held for trading.
Correct: (B) and (D) match the stated investing inflows and outflows, respectively.
Incorrect: statement (C) is not included among the stated investing outflows because the shares are held for trading.

body:
A company issues one debenture with a nominal value of ₹250 for ₹280. Arrange the following steps in the order from determining the issue premium to presenting it in the balance sheet.
(A) Show the premium credited to Securities Premium Reserve on the liabilities side under “Reserves and Surpluses”.
(B) Compare the issue price with the nominal value to establish whether the debenture is issued at a premium.
(C) Determine the premium as ₹30 per debenture.
(D) Credit Securities Premium Reserve with the premium.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: The issue price of ₹280 exceeds the nominal value of ₹250, so the debenture is issued at a premium of ₹30. First establish that the price is above nominal value, then determine the premium, credit Securities Premium Reserve, and show it on the liabilities side under “Reserves and Surpluses”.
evidence_quotes: 2.4.3 Debentures issued at Premium A debenture is said to be issued at a premium when the price charged is more than its nominal value. For example, the issue of Rs. 100 debentures for Rs. 110, (Rs. 10 is being the premium). The amount of premium is credited to Securities Premium Reserve account and is shown on the
liabilities side of the balance sheet under the head “Reserves and Surpluses”.
stated_assumptions: One debenture is issued at the stated issue price; its nominal value is ₹250 and its issue price is ₹280.
The task concerns only the premium on issue, with no other adjustments.
option_analysis: A is incorrect because it places the balance sheet presentation before the credit to Securities Premium Reserve.
B is incorrect because it determines the premium before establishing that the issue price is above nominal value.
C is incorrect because it credits the reserve before determining the amount of premium.
D is correct: compare the issue price with nominal value, determine the excess, credit Securities Premium Reserve, and then show it under the stated balance sheet head.

E1.1 supports identifying the premium and its balance-sheet presentation; E2.3 supports crediting Securities Premium Reserve.

body: At the firm’s last balance sheet date, 31 March 20X5, partner R died on 31 August 20X5. The firm’s profits for the three completed years immediately preceding 31 March 20X5 were ₹2,10,000, ₹2,40,000 and ₹2,70,000. body: Leena and Farah agree orally to enter into a partnership. They have not prepared a written document. Which statement correctly describes whether their agreement must be in writing?
options: Their partnership cannot come into existence until the oral terms are put in writing.
Their oral agreement is itself a Partnership Deed.
Their oral agreement can establish the partnership; a written document is not compulsory.
Their partnership can come into existence without an agreement if they prepare a written deed later.
explanation: A partnership comes into existence as a result of an agreement, which may be oral or written. The agreement is not required to be in writing, so the oral agreement can establish the partnership. A Partnership Deed is the document containing the terms when the agreement is in writing.

body: A firm maintains partners’ accounts under the fixed capital method. During the year, partner R is allocated a share of profit and makes ordinary drawings. No additional capital is introduced, and no part of R’s capital is withdrawn under the partnership agreement. What happens to R’s Capital Account during the year?
options: It is increased by the share of profit allocated to R.
It remains unchanged during the year.
It is reduced by the ordinary drawings made by R.
It is adjusted for both the share of profit and the ordinary drawings.
explanation: Under the fixed capital method, a partner’s capital remains fixed unless additional capital is introduced or part of the capital is withdrawn under the agreement. Neither occurs here, so R’s Capital Account remains unchanged; the share of profit and drawings are recorded in R’s Current Account.
evidence_quotes: (a) Fixed Capital Method: Under the fixed capital method, the capitals of the partners shall remain fixed unless additional capital is introduced or a part of the capital is withdrawn as per the agreement among the partners. All items like share of profit or loss, interest on capital, drawings, interest on drawings,

etc. are recorded in a separate accounts, called Partner’s Current Account. The partners’ capital accounts will always show a credit balance, which shall remain the same (fixed) year after year unless there is any addition or withdrawal of capital. The partners’ current account on the other hand, may show a debit or a

credit balance. Thus under this method, two accounts are maintained for each partner viz., capital account and current account, While the partners’ capital accounts shall always appear on the liabilities side in the balance sheet, the partners’ current account’s balance shall be shown on the liabilities side, if they
have credit balance and on the assets side, if they have debit balance.
stated_assumptions: The firm uses the fixed capital method.
R receives a share of profit and makes ordinary drawings during the year.
No additional capital is introduced and no part of R’s capital is withdrawn under the agreement.
option_analysis: A is incorrect because it records the share of profit and drawings in the Capital Account rather than the Current Account.
B is correct: the Capital Account remains unchanged in the stated circumstances, while the share of profit and drawings are recorded in the Current Account.
C is incorrect because it records the share of profit in the Capital Account.
D is incorrect because drawings are recorded in the Current Account, not omitted from both accounts.

supporting_spans.quote: (a) Fixed Capital Method: Under the fixed capital method, the capitals of the partners shall remain fixed unless additional capital is introduced or a part of the capital is withdrawn as per the agreement among the partners. All items like share of profit or loss, interest on capital, drawings, interest on drawings, etc. are recorded in a separate accounts, called Partner’s Current Account. The partners’ capital accounts will always show a credit balance, which shall remain the same (fixed) year after year unless there is any addition or withdrawal of capital. The partners’ current account on the other hand, may show a debit or a credit

balance. body:
A company issues 500 debentures, each having a nominal value of ₹320, at an issue price of ₹400 per debenture. All 500 debentures are issued at that price. Calculate the premium as a percentage of the total nominal value, using (total premium ÷ total nominal value) × 100. What is the premium percentage?
(A) 25%
(B) 20%
(C) 125%
(D) 80%
explanation: The premium per debenture is ₹400 − ₹320 = ₹80. Thus, the total premium is ₹40,000 and the total nominal value is ₹1,60,000, giving a premium percentage of (₹40,000 ÷ ₹1,60,000) × 100 = 25%.

body:
A company offers 70,000 shares of face value ₹10 each for subscription. Applications are received for 63,000 shares, and all 63,000 shares are allotted. The company calls ₹8 per allotted share. Holders of 3,000 allotted shares do not pay any amount called; all other allottees pay ₹8 per share.

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Issued capital
(B) Subscribed capital
(C) Called-up capital
(D) Paid-up capital

List-II
(I) ₹4,80,000
(II) ₹7,00,000
(III) ₹5,04,000
(IV) ₹6,30,000

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Issued capital is 70,000 × ₹10 = ₹7,00,000, and subscribed capital is 63,000 × ₹10 = ₹6,30,000. Called-up capital is 63,000 × ₹8 = ₹5,04,000. Calls in arrears are 3,000 × ₹8 = ₹24,000, so paid-up capital is ₹5,04,000 − ₹24,000 = ₹4,80,000; these amounts match option D.
evidence_quotes: 4 Accountancy : Company Accounts and Analysis of Financial Statements 1.3.1Categories of Share Capital From accounting point of view the share capital of the company can be classified as follows: • Authorised Capital: Authorised capital is the amount of share capital which a company is authorised to issue by its

Memorandum of Association. The company cannot raise more than the amount of capital as specified in the Memorandum of Association. It is also called Nominal or Registered capital. The authorised capital can be increased or decreased as per the procedure laid down in the Companies Act. It should be noted that the

company need not issue the entire authorised capital for public subscription at a time. Depending upon its requirement, it may issue share capital but in any case, it should not be more than the amount of authorised capital. • Issued Capital: It is that part of the authorised capital which is actually issued to the

public for subscription including the shares allotted to vendors and the signatories to the company’s memorandum. The authorised capital which is not offered for public subscription is known as ‘unissued capital’. Unissued capital may be offered for public subscription at a later date. • Subscribed Capital: It is that

Applications are received for 63,000 shares and exactly 63,000 shares are allotted.
₹8 per allotted share is called up; holders of 3,000 allotted shares pay none of the called amount, and all other allottees pay it in full.
The amounts relate to the stated share capital only; no other calls or amounts affect the calculation.
option_analysis: This swaps issued capital and subscribed capital: the number issued is 70,000, whereas 63,000 shares are subscribed and allotted.
This swaps called-up capital and paid-up capital, failing to deduct the ₹24,000 unpaid on calls from the called-up amount.
This uses the ₹8 called-up amount to calculate subscribed capital and the full ₹10 face value to calculate called-up capital.
Issued capital is 70,000 × ₹10; subscribed capital is 63,000 × ₹10; called-up capital is 63,000 × ₹8; paid-up capital is called-up capital less the unpaid calls on 3,000 shares.

body:
An enterprise is preparing a cash flow statement for an accounting period. Consider the following statements about its presentation.
(A) The statement reports the change in the position of cash and cash equivalents over the accounting period.
(B) Activities contributing to this change are classified as operating, investing and financing activities.
(C) Under each activity heading, it is sufficient to show only the net cash flow (or use), rather than full details of inflows and outflows.
(D) The aggregate net cash flow (or use) is worked out from the net amounts of the operating, investing and financing activities.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A cash flow statement reports changes in cash and cash equivalents over an accounting period and classifies contributing activities as operating, investing and financing. It gives full details of inflows and outflows under these heads, including the net cash flow or use; the aggregate is worked out from the activities. Therefore, A, B and D are correct, while C is inconsistent with the required presentation.
evidence_quotes: working out the net cash flow (or use) from all the three activities for an accounting period has been explained in details and a brief format of Cash Flow Statement has also been given in Exhibit 6.2. However, while preparing a cash flow statement, full details of inflows and outflows are given under these heads

including the net cash flow (or use). The aggregate of the net ‘cash flows (or use) is worked out and is shown as ‘Net Increase/Decrease in cash and Cash Equivalents’ to which the amount of ‘cash and cash equivalent at the beginning’ is added and thus the amount of ‘cash and cash equivalents at the end’ is arrived at
stated_assumptions: The question concerns the presentation of a cash flow statement for one accounting period.
The listed activities are the operating, investing and financing activities contributing to the change in cash and cash equivalents.
option_analysis: Incorrect: this choice includes C, which conflicts with the requirement to give full details of inflows and outflows, and omits D.

body:
An analyst is preparing a common-size balance sheet for two years. Arrange these actions in the correct sequence:
(A) Work out each item’s percentage of its relevant total.
(B) List the absolute rupee figures for the two years.
(C) Choose the applicable common base of 100: total assets for asset items and total liabilities for liability items.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: First list the absolute rupee figures for the two years, then choose the common base, and finally calculate each item’s percentage of that base. Therefore, the correct sequence is (B), (C), (A).

component percentage statement, is a financial tool for studying the key changes and trends in the financial position and operational result of a company. Here, each item in the statement is stated as a percentage of the aggregate, or revenue from operations of which that item is a part. For example, a common size

balance sheet shows the percentage of each asset to the total assets, and that of each liability to the total liabilities. Similarly, in the common size statement of profit and loss, the items of expenditure are shown as a percentage of the revenue from operations. If such a statement is prepared for successive

periods, it shows the changes of the respective percentages over a period of time. Common size analysis is of immense use for comparing enterprises which differ substantially in size as it provides an insight into the structure of financial statements. body: A, B, C and D continue as partners; no partner is admitted or retires. Their old profit-sharing ratio is 5:3:2:2, and their agreed new ratio is 7:5:4:2. The firm has goodwill, and its value is to be adjusted for the change in ratio. Which treatment correctly identifies the sacrificing and gaining partners and records the goodwill adjustment?
options: A and D are sacrificing partners and B and C are gaining partners; credit A and D, and debit B and C.
A and D are gaining partners and B and C are sacrificing partners; debit A and D, and credit B and C.
A, B and C are gaining partners and D is unchanged; debit A, B and C, and leave D unadjusted.
A and D are sacrificing partners and B and C are gaining partners; debit A and D, and credit B and C.
explanation: The old shares, expressed with denominator 36, are A 15/36, B 9/36, C 6/36 and D 6/36; the new shares are A 14/36, B 10/36, C 8/36 and D 4/36. A and D therefore sacrifice shares, while B and C gain shares. The goodwill adjustment credits the sacrificing partners and debits the gaining partners.

body: A new partner pays a cash premium for goodwill directly to the existing partners, privately. The firm does not receive or record the payment. What should the firm record in its books for this payment?
options: No journal entry should be passed.
Debit Bank A/c and credit Premium for Goodwill A/c.
Debit Goodwill A/c and credit the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts.
Debit the new partner’s capital account and credit the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts.
explanation: Because the new partner pays the premium directly to the existing partners privately, no entry is passed in the firm’s books. The other entries relate to goodwill amounts handled through the firm, not to the private payment described here.
evidence_quotes: 2.5.5 Treatment of Goodwill As stated earlier, the incoming partner who acquires his share in the profits of the firm from the existing partners brings in additional amount to compensate them for loss of their share in super profits. It is termed as his share of goodwill (also called premium for goodwill). 2.5.5.1 When

the new Partner brings goodwill in cash. The amount of premium brought in by the new partner is shared by the existing partners in their ratio of sacrifice. If this amount is paid to the old partners directly (privately) by the new partner, no entry is passed in the books of the firm. But, when the amount is paid

through the firm, which is generally the case, the following journal entries are passed: (i) Bank A/c Dr. To Premium for Goodwill A/c (Amount brought by new partner as premium) (ii) Goodwill A/c Dr. To Sacrificing Partners Capital A/c (Individually)(Goodwill distributed among the existing partners’ in their

sacrificing ratio). Alternatively, it is credited to the new partner’s capital account and then adjusted in favour of the existing partners in their sacrificing ratio. In that case the journal entries will be as follows: Reprint 2026-27
stated_assumptions: The amount is a cash premium for goodwill paid directly and privately by the incoming partner to the existing partners.
The firm does not receive the payment, and no other transaction relating to the premium is recorded by the firm.
option_analysis: Correct: the premium is paid directly to the existing partners privately, so no entry is passed in the firm’s books.
Incorrect: the Bank A/c and Premium for Goodwill A/c entry applies when the premium is paid through the firm.
Incorrect: this entry records distribution of goodwill handled through the firm, whereas the stated payment is private.
Incorrect: this capital-account adjustment is an alternative treatment for goodwill handled through the firm, not for the stated private payment.

body: Company Z, the issuer, initially issues a security to investor A. Later, A sells the same security to investor B. A and B are investors, and Company Z is not a party to the later sale. How should the later sale be classified?
options: It is a secondary-market transaction because the issuer was involved when A first obtained the security.
It is a secondary-market transaction because A sells the security to another investor rather than to the issuer.
It is not a secondary-market transaction because A, rather than the issuer, is the seller.
It is not a secondary-market transaction because the issuer is not a party to the later sale.
explanation: The later sale is between investor A and investor B, so the security is sold from one investor to another rather than to the issuer. The issuer’s involvement in the earlier issue does not change who the parties are to this later sale.
evidence_quotes: The Secondary Market is a place where an investor can buy/sell shares or securities from another investor rather than the issuer.
stated_assumptions: Company Z is the issuer of the security.
A and B are investors.
A sells the same security to B in the later transaction.
Company Z is not a party to the later transaction.
option_analysis: A is incorrect because the classification of the later sale depends on its parties, not on the issuer’s involvement in the earlier issue.
B is correct because the later sale is from investor A to investor B rather than to the issuer.
C is incorrect because an investor can sell a security to another investor in a secondary-market transaction.
D is incorrect because the stated definition identifies an investor-to-investor sale as secondary; the issuer need not be a party to that sale.

body:
A company must choose exactly one of three mutually exclusive alternatives. The finance team estimates their effects on the current market value of equity shares, including all relevant costs and benefits, on the same basis: A, +₹8 lakh; B, +₹5 lakh; C, –₹12 lakh. Assume these estimates are reliable. Consider the following statements:
(A) Alternative A is the best choice for maximising shareholders’ wealth among these alternatives.
(B) Alternative B is equally good as A because both are projected to increase market value.
(C) Alternative C is the best choice because its projected change has the greatest absolute size.
(D) Selecting the best available alternative makes the decision efficient.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Alternative A gives the greatest increase in market value of equity shares, so it is the best choice for maximising shareholders’ wealth among the stated alternatives. Decision-making is efficient when the best available alternative is selected. B’s increase is smaller, while C’s change is a decrease.

supporting_spans.quote: FINANCIAL MANAGEMENTS 219 BUSINESS STUDIES 218 is linked to the three basic financial decisions which you will study a little later. This is because a company funds belong to the shareholders and the manner in which they are invested and the return earned by them determines their market value and price. It means maximisation of the market value of equity shares. The market price of equity share increases, if the benefit from a decision exceeds the cost involved. All financial decisions aim at ensuring that each decision is efficient and adds some value. Such value additions tend to increase the market price of shares. Therefore, those

financial decisions are taken which will ultimately prove gainful from the point of view of the shareholders. The shareholders gain if the value of shares in the market increases. Those decisions which result in decline in the share price are poor financial decisions. Thus, we can say, the objective of financial management is to maximise the current price of equity shares of the company or to maximise the wealth of owners of the company, that is, the shareholders. Therefore, when a decision is taken about investment in a new machine, the aim of financial management is to ensure that benefits from the investment exceed the cost so that some

value addition takes place. Similarly, when finance is procured, the aim is to reduce the cost so that the value addition is even higher. In fact, in all financial decisions, major or minor, the ultimate objective that guides the decision-maker is that some value addition should take place. All those avenues of investment, modes of financing, ways of handling various components of working capital must be identified which will ultimately lead to an increase in the price of equity share. It can happen through efficient decision-making. Decision-making is efficient if, out of the various available alternatives, the best is selected. Financial

body:
Use this stated objective: “One of the main objectives of the primary market is to allow companies to raise capital through the issuance of securities.” Match each statement in List-I with its interpretation in List-II.

List-I
(A) Companies may raise capital through the issuance of securities.
(B) Every company seeking to raise capital must issue securities.
(C) Issuance of securities is the sole route by which companies can raise capital.
(D) Issuing securities cannot enable companies to raise capital.

List-II
(I) Expresses the stated enabling link.
(II) Claims that securities issuance is necessary whenever a company seeks capital.
(III) Claims that securities issuance is the only route to raise capital.
(IV) Denies the stated enabling link.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The stated objective identifies securities issuance as a way for companies to raise capital, so (A) expresses the enabling link. The objective does not establish that companies must use this route or that it is the only route. Statement (D) denies the stated link.
evidence_quotes: One of the main objectives of the primary market is to allow companies to raise capital through the issuance of securities
stated_assumptions: Treat “may” and “can” as expressing possibility, “must” as expressing necessity, and “only” as expressing exclusivity.
Classify each statement solely against the objective quoted in the stem.
option_analysis: Incorrect: this assigns the direct enabling link to the necessity claim in (B), rather than to (A).
Incorrect: this treats the necessity claim in (B) as exclusivity and the exclusivity claim in (C) as necessity.
Correct: (A) states the enabling link, (B) adds necessity, (C) adds exclusivity, and (D) denies the link.
Incorrect: this classifies the denial in (D) as an exclusivity claim and the exclusivity claim in (C) as a denial.

body:
A firm serves customers at several locations and is deciding how many warehouses to operate. It also stores a product that requires long-term storage. Consider the following statements:
(A) Warehousing may be needed when the time of production differs from the time the product is required for consumption.
(B) Increasing the number of warehouses generally reduces the time taken to serve customers at different locations but increases warehousing cost.
(C) To minimise transportation charges for the long-term-storage product, the firm should locate its warehouses near the markets.
(D) The firm should balance warehousing cost against the level of customer service when deciding on its warehouses.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Statements (A), (B) and (D) match the stated warehousing need, the general relationship between warehouse numbers, service time and cost, and the need to balance cost with customer service. Statement (C) is incorrect: for products requiring long-term storage, locating warehouses near production sites helps minimise transportation charges.
evidence_quotes: consumption. Generally the efficiency of a firm in serving its customers will depend on where these warehouses are located and where are these to be delivered. Generally larger the number of warehouses a firm has, lesser would be the time taken in serving customers at different locations but greater would be the cost

of warehousing and vice-versa. Thus the firm has to strike a balance between the cost of warehousing and the level of customer service. For products requiring long- term storage (such as agricultural products) the warehouses are located near production sites. This helps in minimising the charges on transportation of
stated_assumptions: The firm serves customers at several locations.
The product considered for the location decision requires long-term storage.

body:
Company Q is the issuer of the shares. It first issues shares to Aruna, an investor. Later, Aruna transfers part of her holding to Bala, an investor; Bala transfers some of those shares to Charu, an investor; and Charu sells shares to Company Q. Each transaction is direct between the named parties, and each concerns shares. Match each transaction in List-I with its description in List-II. Determine only whether each transaction fits the secondary-market definition.
List-I
(A) Company Q first issues shares to Aruna.
(B) Aruna transfers shares to Bala.
(C) Bala transfers shares to Charu.
(D) Charu sells shares to Company Q.
List-II
(I) The issuer supplies shares to an investor; the transaction is not between investors.
(II) Aruna supplies shares to Bala; both are investors.
(III) Bala supplies shares to Charu; both are investors.
(IV) Charu supplies shares to the issuer; the transaction is not between investors.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The stated definition describes secondary-market dealings as an investor buying or selling shares from another investor rather than the issuer. The transfers from Aruna to Bala and from Bala to Charu are between investors, while the initial issue is from the issuer and Charu’s sale is to the issuer. The party-specific descriptions distinguish the two investor-to-investor transfers, giving the mapping in option D.
evidence_quotes: The Secondary Market is a place where an investor can buy/sell shares or securities from another investor rather than the issuer.
stated_assumptions: Company Q is the issuer; Aruna, Bala and Charu are investors.
Each transaction concerns shares and is direct between the named parties; no other party is the buyer or seller.
The task is to identify which transactions fit the stated secondary-market definition; no other market classification is required.
option_analysis: Incorrect: it reverses the descriptions for the two successive transfers, although Aruna sells to Bala before Bala sells to Charu.
Incorrect: it assigns the issuer-as-recipient description to the initial issue and the issuer-as-supplier description to Charu’s sale, contrary to the stated transaction directions.
Incorrect: it treats the initial issue as a transaction between investors and Aruna’s transfer to Bala as a transaction involving the issuer.
Correct: the initial issue is from the issuer to an investor, the two later transfers are between investors, and Charu’s sale is to the issuer.

body: A firm has procured ₹20,00,000 for one year at an annual procurement cost of ₹1,60,000. It will invest the entire amount in exactly one of four projects. The stated annual investment returns are: Project P, ₹1,80,000; Project Q, ₹1,60,000; Project R, ₹1,55,000; and Project S, ₹1,50,000. Assume these are directly comparable annual amounts. Which project meets the condition that the return from the investment exceeds the cost of procuring the finance?
explanation: Project P’s annual return of ₹1,80,000 exceeds the annual procurement cost of ₹1,60,000. Project Q’s return equals the cost, while Projects R and S return less than the cost.
evidence_quotes: For optimal procurement, different available sources of finance are identified and compared in terms of their costs and associated risks. Similarly, the finance so procured needs to be invested in a manner that the returns from the investment exceed the cost at which procurement has taken place. Financial Management
stated_assumptions: The finance is procured for one year, and the stated procurement cost and project returns are annual amounts.
The entire ₹20,00,000 is invested in exactly one project; the stated returns are directly comparable with the procurement cost.
The question tests only whether the investment return exceeds the cost of procuring the finance.
option_analysis: Project P is correct because its annual return of ₹1,80,000 is greater than the annual procurement cost of ₹1,60,000.
Project Q is incorrect because its annual return equals, rather than exceeds, the procurement cost.
Project R is incorrect because its annual return of ₹1,55,000 is below the procurement cost.
Project S is incorrect because its annual return of ₹1,50,000 is below the procurement cost.

P is occupying the post for which P was selected, while Q has not begun occupying the post for which Q was selected. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both employees have undergone orientation; placement has occurred for P only.
Only P has undergone orientation; placement has occurred for both P and Q.

explanation: Both employees have undergone orientation because each was introduced to other employees and familiarised with the organisation’s rules and policies. Placement has occurred for P only, because P is occupying the selected post and Q has not begun occupying Q’s selected post.

A case includes a government-owned organisation, a privately owned business, a small business and a company with big plans. Consider the following statements about planning:
(A) Planning is required in both government-owned and privately owned organisations.
(B) Planning is relevant to both a small business and a company with big plans.
(C) Planning is required only in privately owned organisations.
(D) A small business needs plans only if it operates nationwide.
Select the correct statements.
explanation: The excerpt states that organisations, including government-owned and privately owned ones, require planning. It also says that a small business has its own plans and that other companies have big plans. Therefore, (A) and (B) are correct; (C) and (D) impose restrictions that the stated principle does not support.

body:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct mapping for each transaction.
List-I
(A) Zenith Ltd issues a batch of shares directly to Riya.
(B) Riya sells the shares she received to Samir.
(C) Samir sells those same shares to Tara.
(D) Zenith Ltd issues a separate batch of shares directly to Tara.
List-II
(I) Secondary-market acquisition by Tara from Samir.
(II) Secondary-market acquisition by Samir from Riya.
(III) Riya’s direct acquisition from Zenith Ltd.
(IV) Tara’s direct acquisition from Zenith Ltd.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Riya receives the first batch directly from Zenith Ltd, so her acquisition is not from another investor. Samir acquires the shares from Riya, and Tara then acquires those shares from Samir; both are investor-to-investor transactions. Tara’s acquisition of the separate batch is directly from the issuer.
evidence_quotes: The Secondary Market is a place where an investor can buy/sell shares or securities from another investor rather than the issuer.
stated_assumptions: Riya, Samir and Tara are investors, and Zenith Ltd is the issuer.
The shares in transactions (B) and (C) are the same shares first issued to Riya; Zenith Ltd issues a separate batch directly to Tara in (D).
In each transaction, the stated seller or issuer is the immediate source of the recipient’s shares.
option_analysis: Correct. Riya acquires directly from the issuer; Samir acquires from Riya; Tara acquires those shares from Samir; and Tara’s separate batch comes directly from the issuer.
Incorrect. This assigns Samir’s acquisition from Riya to Riya’s direct acquisition from the issuer, and assigns Riya’s acquisition to a secondary-market acquisition by Samir.
Incorrect. This swaps the two investor-to-investor acquisitions: Samir acquires from Riya, while Tara acquires from Samir.
Incorrect. This treats Tara’s purchase from Samir as a direct acquisition from the issuer and her separate direct acquisition from Zenith Ltd as an investor-to-investor acquisition.

body:
A company is considering taking additional debt. The new debt will create regular interest payments and a principal repayment obligation. Which projected-cash check directly addresses the outflows created by this borrowing?

A. Confirm that projected cash will cover the added interest payments and principal repayment.
B. Confirm that projected cash will cover the added interest payments but exclude principal repayment.
C. Confirm that projected cash will cover the added principal repayment but exclude interest payments.
D. Confirm that projected cash will cover normal operations but exclude both debt payments.
options: Confirm that projected cash will cover the added interest payments and principal repayment.
Confirm that projected cash will cover the added interest payments but exclude principal repayment.
Confirm that projected cash will cover the added principal repayment but exclude interest payments.
Confirm that projected cash will cover normal operations but exclude both debt payments.
explanation: Additional debt creates increased outflows, and debt requires regular interest payments and repayment of principal. The company should therefore check that projected cash can meet both added obligations; the other choices leave out at least one of these debt payments.
evidence_quotes: Financial ManageMents 231 BUsiness st UDies 230 factors. For example, debt requires regular servicing. Interest payment and repayment of principal are obligatory on a business. In addition a company planning to raise debt must have sufficient cash to meet the increased outflows because of higher debt. Similarly,
stated_assumptions: The proposed financing is additional debt.
The new debt entails regular interest payments and repayment of principal.
The question asks which projected-cash check addresses the outflows created by that debt.
option_analysis: A is correct: it includes both interest payments and principal repayment, the obligations specified in the stem.
B is incorrect: it excludes principal repayment, which the stem states is an obligation of the new debt.
C is incorrect: it excludes interest payments, which the stem states are an obligation of the new debt.
D is incorrect: it excludes both debt payments, so it does not address the outflows created by the borrowing.

supporting_spans.quote: Financial ManageMents 231 BUsiness st UDies 230 factors. For example, debt requires regular servicing. Interest payment and repayment of principal are obligatory on a business. In addition a company planning to raise debt must have sufficient cash to meet the increased outflows because of higher debt. Similarly, important factors which determine the choice of capital structure are as follows: 1. Cash Flow Position: Size of projected cash flows must be considered before borrowing. Cash flows must not only cover fixed cash payment obligations but there must be sufficient buffer also. It must be kept in mind that a company has cash payment

obligations for (i) normal business operations; (ii) for investment in fixed assets; and (iii) for meeting the debt service commitments i.e., payment of interest and repayment of principal. 2. Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR): The interest coverage ratio refers to the number of times earnings before interest and taxes of a company covers the interest obligation. This may be calculated as follows: ICR = EBIT Interest The higher the ratio, lower shall be the risk of company failing to meet its interest payment obligations. However, this ratio is not an adequate measure. A firm may have a high EBIT but low cash balance. Apart from interest,

repayment obligations are also relevant. 3. Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR): Debt Service Coverage Ratio takes care of the deficiencies referred to in the Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR). The cash profits generated by the operations are compared with the total cash required for the service of the debt and the preference share capital. It is calculated as follows: Profit after tax + Depreciation + Interest + Non Cash exp. Pref. Div + Interest + Repayment obligation a higher DSCR indicates better ability to meet cash commitments and consequently, the company’s potential to increase debt component in its capital structure. 4. body: A manufacturer sells its product through independent local dealers and wants to improve its availability to target customers through this network. It must choose one action. Which action is a Place or physical-distribution decision for this objective?
options: Select local dealers and support them with discounts and promotional campaigns.
Choose an advertising message and media to communicate product features to target customers.
Set a product price that buyers perceive to be in line with its value.
Plan the functional, psychological and social benefits the product will provide.
explanation: Place or physical distribution includes activities that make products available to target customers, including selecting dealers and supporting intermediaries with discounts or promotional campaigns. Selecting and supporting local dealers therefore addresses availability through the stated network. The other choices concern communicating product features, setting price and planning product benefits.

stated_assumptions: The discounts and promotional-campaign support in option A are directed to dealers; the advertising in option B is directed to target customers.
Each option describes one action, and the question asks which action addresses availability through the dealer network.

D is incorrect: this action concerns the benefits planned for the product rather than the dealer network.

supporting_spans.quote: BUSINe SS STUDIe S 256 perceive the price to be in line with the value of the product. 3. Place: Place or Physical Distribution include activities that make firm’s products available to the target customers. Important decision areas in this respect include selection of dealers or intermediaries to reach the customers, providing support to the intermediaries (by way of discounts, promotional campaigns, etc.). The intermediaries in turn keep inventory of the firm’s products, demonstrate them to potential buyers, negotiate price with buyers, close sales and also service the products after the sale. The other decision areas relate to managing

inventory, storage and warehousing and transportation of goods from the place it is produced to the place it is required by the buyers. 4. Promotion: Promotion of products and services include activities that communicate availability, features, merits, etc., of the products to the target customers and persuade them to buy it. Most marketing organisations, undertake various promotional activities and spend substantial amount of money on the promotion of their goods through using number of tools such as advertising, personal selling and sales promotion techniques (like price discounts, free samples, etc.). A large number of decisions are to be

taken in each of the area specified above. For example, in the respect of advertising it is important to decide about the message, the media to be used (example, print-media– newspaper, magazines, the objections of customers, etc.). The success of a market offer will depend on how well these ingredients are mixed to create superior value for the customers and simultaneously achieve their sale and profit objectives. Let us say a firm would like to achieve necessary volume of sale at a cost that will permit a desired level of profit. But so many alternative mixes can be adopted by a firm to achieve this objectives. The issue before a firm then

is to decide what would be the most effective combination of elements to achieve the given objectives. proDuCTs From the customer’s point of view, a product is a bundle of utilities, which is purchased because of its capability to provide satisfaction of certain need. A buyer buys a product or service for what it does for her or the benefit it provides to her. There can be three types of benefits a customer may seek to satisfy from the purchase of a product, viz., (i) functional benefits, (ii) psychological benefits, and (iii) social benefits. For example, the purchase of a motorcycle provides functional utility of transportation, but at the

same time satisfies the need for prestige and esteem and provides social benefit by the way of acceptance from a group, by riding a motorbike. Thus, all these aspects should be considered while planning for a product. Ch_10.indd 256 10-08-2022 10:04:27 Reprint 2026-27

body:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Management ensures that an organisation earns enough revenue to cover its costs.
(B) Management ensures that the organisation makes a profit.
(C) Management exploits the organisation’s growth potential to remain in the industry.
(D) The organisation’s main objective is to use human and material resources to the maximum possible advantage.
List-II
(I) Main objective of the organisation
(II) Survival
(III) Profit
(IV) Growth
Each entry in List-II is to be used once.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Earning enough revenue to cover costs identifies survival, while ensuring that the organisation makes a profit identifies profit. Exploiting growth potential to remain in the industry identifies growth, and maximum advantage from using human and material resources is the organisation’s main objective. Thus, option B gives the correct one-to-one matches.
evidence_quotes: The m ain objective of any organisation should be to utilise human and material resources to the maximum possible advantage, i.e., to fulfill the economic objectives of a business. These are survival, profit and growth. Survival: The basic objectives of any business is survival. Management must strive to ensure the

survival of the organisation. In order to survive, an organisation must earn enough revenues to cover costs. Pro fit: Mere survival is not enough for business. Management has to ensure that the organisation makes a profit. Profit provides a vital incentive for the continued successful operation of the enterprise.

10 Business Studies Growth: A business needs to add to its prospects in the long run, for this it is important for the business to grow. To remain in the industry, management must exploit fully the growth potential of the organisation.
stated_assumptions: Each List-I description is to be matched with its single corresponding entry in List-II; every List-II entry is used once.
option_analysis: Incorrect: this swaps survival, which involves earning enough revenue to cover costs, with profit.
Correct: all four descriptions are matched to their corresponding objective or main objective.
Incorrect: this treats the growth objective as the main objective and the resource-utilisation objective as growth.
Incorrect: this swaps profit with growth.

body: A company needs funds for its own expansion and is comparing the following plans. Which plan most directly fits the objective of the company raising capital through the issuance of securities?
options: Borrow funds from a bank, which transfers the loan directly to the company.
Sell an unused machine, with the buyer transferring the price directly to the company.
Issue new securities to applicants, who transfer their subscription funds directly to the company.
Have the founders sell some of their existing holdings, with buyers transferring the price to the founders.
explanation: The stated objective combines two conditions: the company raises funds, and it does so through issuing securities. In option C, the company issues securities and receives the subscription funds. Options A and B provide funds through a loan and an asset sale, while option D directs the proceeds to the founders.
evidence_quotes: One of the main objectives of the primary market is to allow companies to raise capital through the issuance of securities
stated_assumptions: The company, rather than its founders, needs funds for its expansion.
Each plan is carried out exactly as described, and the stated recipient receives the funds.
The criterion is that the company receives funds through its own issuance of securities.
option_analysis: A: The company receives funds, but the plan specifies a bank loan rather than an issuance of securities.
B: The company receives funds from an asset sale, not through an issuance of securities.
C: The company issues securities and receives the subscription funds, meeting both conditions.
D: The proceeds go to the founders, and the plan describes a sale of their existing holdings rather than an issuance by the company.

(A) Toothpaste benefits such as whitening teeth and strengthening gums are part of the product concept.
(B) For a refrigerator, after-sales services, handling complaints and availability of spare parts can be part of the extended product.
(C) Because a refrigerator is a physical good, its product concept excludes after-sales services and availability of spare parts.
(D) The extended-product aspect is particularly important for consumer durables such as refrigerators.

explanation: The product concept includes customer benefits in addition to the physical product, and it can also include after-sales services, complaint handling and spare-parts availability as extended product. body:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Science, not the rule of thumb
(B) Harmony, not discord
(C) Cooperation, not individualism
(D) Development of each person to greatest efficiency and prosperity
List-II
(I) A manager rejects a method chosen solely because it is customary and selects one supported by scientific study.
(II) Managers and workers seek harmonious relations rather than discord.
(III) Workers and managers coordinate their efforts instead of acting individually.
(IV) A manager develops each employee towards the greatest efficiency and prosperity.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The customary method is contrasted with a scientifically supported method, matching science rather than the rule of thumb. The other cases correspond respectively to harmony, cooperation, and developing each person to greatest efficiency and prosperity.
evidence_quotes: 64 Business Studies Summary Meaning Principles of management are general guidelines, which can be used for conduct in work places under certain situations. They help managers to take and implement decisions. Nature The nature of management principles can be discussed under the heads- formed by practice; general

guidelines; universal; flexible; behavioural; contingent; and cause and effect relationship Significance Proper understanding of significance of management principles is essential to make sound decisions by managers. The significance can be discussed under the following heads- Increase in efficiency; Optimum

utilisation of resources; Scientific decision making; Adaptation to changing environment; Fulfilling social responsibilities; Proper research and development; Training managers; and Effective administration. Scientific Management Taylor’s principles of scientific management are — Science, not the rule of thumb;

Harmony not discord; Cooperation not individualism; Maximum not restricted output; Development of each person to her/ his greatest efficiency and prosperity. The techniques of scientific management as per Taylor were — Functional foremanship; Standardisation and simplification of work; Fatigue Study; Method Study;
stated_assumptions: Each case is an independent example, and the stated action is the basis for matching it to one Taylor principle.
option_analysis: Incorrect: it interchanges the cases of harmony and cooperation. The case about harmonious relations matches harmony, while coordinated effort rather than individual action matches cooperation.
Incorrect: the case about harmonious relations does not illustrate science rather than the rule of thumb, and the customary-method case does not illustrate harmony rather than discord.
Incorrect: it interchanges cooperation and development. Coordinated effort rather than individual action matches cooperation, while developing each employee matches development.
Correct: each case is paired with the Taylor principle it describes.

body:
Arrange the following actions in the order in which they move from top management towards the workforce:
(i) Supervisors pass instructions from middle management to workers.
(ii) Top management formulates overall organisational goals and strategies.
(iii) Middle management interprets top management’s policies and carries out its plans.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Top management formulates overall organisational goals and strategies. Middle management interprets top management’s policies and carries out its plans, while supervisors pass middle management’s instructions to workers. Therefore, the order from top management towards the workforce is (ii)-(iii)-(i).

body:
During calendar year 2026, a factory had 222 machines on 1 January and 240 machines on 31 December. It added 35 machines and removed 17 machines during the year; these were the only changes to its machine stock. Match each item in List-I with its interpretation in List-II.
List-I
(A) 222 machines on 1 January 2026
(B) 240 machines on 31 December 2026
(C) 35 machines added during 2026
(D) An 18-machine net increase between 1 January and 31 December 2026
List-II
(I) Stock measured at the opening date
(II) Flow measuring additions over the year
(III) Stock measured at the closing date
(IV) Flow measuring the change in stock over the year
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The counts of 222 machines on 1 January and 240 on 31 December are stocks because each is measured at a particular point in time. The 35 additions are a flow over the year, and the net change is 240 − 222 = 18 machines, also a flow because it measures a change over a period. The 35 additions and the 18-machine net increase are different measures.
evidence_quotes: Stocks are defined at a particular point of time. However we can measure a change in stock over a specific period of time like how many machines wer e added this year . Such changes in stocks are thus flows, which can be measured over specific time periods.
stated_assumptions: The machine counts are exact and refer to the same factory on the stated dates.
The 35 additions and 17 removals are the only changes to the machine stock during 2026.
An 18-machine net increase is the difference between the closing count of 240 and the opening count of 222.
option_analysis: Option A incorrectly treats the closing count as a flow and the net change over the year as a stock.
Option B correctly matches the two point-in-time counts to stocks and the additions and net change over the year to flows.
Option C incorrectly treats the opening count as a flow and the additions during the year as a stock.
Option D confuses the 35 machines added with the 18-machine net change; both are flows, but they measure different amounts.

Arrange the statements in an explanatory sequence that begins with the institutional context and identification of the arrangement, proceeds to its composition and the roles of its two components, and ends with its alternative name.
(A) The flexible exchange-rate system provides the "float" part, while the fixed-rate system provides the "managed" part.
(B) The arrangement is also called "dirty floating".
(C) Without a formal international agreement, the world has moved to a system best described as managed floating.
(D) The system is a mixture of a flexible exchange-rate system and a fixed-rate system.
Choose the correct sequence:
explanation: The sequence is (C)-(D)-(A)-(B): it introduces the context and arrangement, describes the system as a mixture, explains the roles of the two components, and gives the alternative name. This follows the explanatory order specified in the question.

floating, central banks intervene to buy and sell foreign currencies in an attempt to moderate exchange rate movements whenever they feel that such actions are appropriate. Official reserve transactions are, therefore, not equal to zero.

body: A profit-maximising firm operates in the short run. Its minimum AVC is ₹7 per unit. Its SMC schedule has a descending branch with SMC values ₹16, ₹12 and ₹9 per unit at outputs 1, 2 and 3 units, respectively, and a rising branch with SMC values ₹9, ₹12 and ₹16 per unit at outputs 5, 6 and 7 units, respectively. All listed outputs are feasible, and the firm’s short-run supply curve comprises the rising part of SMC at prices from and above minimum AVC. body: In 2004–05, India’s exports to China were ₹25,232 crore and imports from China were ₹31,892 crore. In 2024–25, the corresponding values were ₹1,20,617 crore and ₹9,59,666 crore. For each year, calculate exports ÷ imports × 100, rounding the resulting ratios to one decimal place. By how many percentage points did India’s exports to China as a percentage of its imports from China change from 2004–05 to 2024–25?
explanation: The export-to-import ratios are (₹25,232 ÷ ₹31,892) × 100 = 79.1% and (₹1,20,617 ÷ ₹9,59,666) × 100 = 12.6%. The change is 12.6 − 79.1 = −66.5 percentage points, so the ratio decreased by 66.5 percentage points. The 84.1 figure is a relative percentage decrease, not a percentage-point decrease.

body:
A report writer is arranging the reasoning that explains the third element of the Balance of Payments (BoP). Arrange the steps in a logical order, beginning with the current and capital accounts.
(A) Set out the current and capital accounts as the BoP elements already named in the description.
(B) Note that it is difficult to record all international transactions accurately.
(C) Introduce an additional, third BoP element to reflect the recording difficulty.
(D) Name that third element errors and omissions.
Choose the correct sequence:
explanation: Begin with the current and capital accounts, then recognise the difficulty of recording all international transactions accurately. The BoP includes a third element, errors and omissions, which reflects that difficulty.
evidence_quotes: Errors and Omissions It is difficult to record all international transactions accurately. Thus, we have a third element of BoP (apart from the current and capital accounts) called errors and omissions which reflects this.
stated_assumptions: The requested order is a logical explanation of the third element, not a chronology of actual international transactions.
No numerical values or additional BoP components are involved.
option_analysis: This starts with the recording difficulty rather than the current and capital accounts specified as the starting point.
This introduces the third element before establishing the recording difficulty it reflects.
This does not begin with the current and capital accounts and places the cause after naming the element.
This gives the logical order: identify the current and capital accounts, recognise the recording difficulty, introduce a third element, and name it errors and omissions.
